newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil products outlook - strike impact lingers.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil products outlook - strike impact lingers.

text.p: The strike at Elf's French refineries may have ended but the aftershock will still be felt this week, oil traders said.

The company drained up to 150,000 tonnes of gasoline from the market and early indications on Monday are of price gains underpinned by U.S. demand. Gas oil also looks tight after recent short-covering induced by the French strike.
Fuel oil, however, will lick its wounds after sharp drops amid a looming prospect of American fuel flooding into Europe.

Shell's Deer Park coking unit in the U.S. is down for three weeks forcing an extra 165,000 tonnes of fuel onto the market. The arbitrage from the U.S. to Europe is open and a large parcel of over 50,000 tonnes is headed into ARA. "That's not good news for high sulphur fuel in NWE," said one trader.
An outage at Star's Louisiana coker unit which uses 5,000-6,000 tonnes of fuel a day was also bearish, although it was not clear how long the unit would be out of commission.
High sulphur cracked prices in Europe are also under pressure from good supplies and there is little reason for prices to break $120 cif NWE, after a deal last week at $119.
But material needed for the Turkish and Portuguese tenders will help keep prices dropping sharply.
Strong U.S. natural gas prices may result in American utilities picking up the surplus low sulphur fuel.

"If U.S. fuel does come to Europe, it probably won't be low sulphur," said one trader. Supplies in the north will remain tightish and end-user demand discreet but prices were not likely to move above the mid $130s fob NWE.
Traders are bullish on gas oil, pointing to last week's French strike and tightness in NWE.
"A lot of production has been lost already. It all needs replacing -- and in the middle of winter," a trader said.
Traders estimated the strike has led to a shortfall of about 200,000 tonnes of gas oil, which Elf has replaced from purchases from other French refiners who have drawn on their own stocks.
Premiums could firm by up to $2 a tonne to Dec IPE +$10 this week as those refiners buy product to cover their shortfall and to comply with minimum end-year stock regulations.
Traders say fob-cif differentials could expand to about $12 lifting low sulphur diesel premiums by $2 to around Dec +$19.
An open arbitrage from Europe to the U.S. should support European gasoline prices after heavy buying from Elf drained as much as 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes out of the market.

"In the Italian islands, there is nothing available for December so the next spot deal may be for early January," said a trader, adding stocks were being run down for year-end tax purposes. NWE barges are expected to fall slightly as refiners take advantage of rich crack spreads to boost gasoline output.
The crack spread could drop to about $2.50-$3.00 from over $3.00 last week but one trader said, "There is a good bottom in this market, once the cracks come down a bit."
